issues.title: b4w.ps1 fails on Linux due to Windows line endings in shebang

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 help
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The script should execute via pwsh and print help, as the task instructions direct.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Error: /usr/bin/env: 'pwsh\r': No such file or directory. The carriage return in the CRLF line ending makes the shebang reference 'pwsh\r' instead of 'pwsh', and env cannot find it.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: b4w.ps1 uses Windows CRLF line endings. The first line `#!/usr/bin/env pwsh\r\n` is parsed by the Linux kernel as requesting an interpreter named `pwsh<CR>`, which doesn't exist. Even if line endings were fixed, `pwsh` may not be on the default PATH — /usr/bin/env may not find pwsh installed at /opt/microsoft/powershell/7/pwsh.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: b4w.ps1:1 — shebang line has CRLF
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Convert b4w.ps1 to LF line endings (git attributes or .editorconfig)
- Or document that b4w.ps1 is Windows-only and b4w.sh is the cross-platform wrapper
- Update task/evaluation templates that instruct users to run `./b4w.ps1` to check platform and suggest `./b4w.sh` on Linux/macOS
- Update CLAUDE.md to note that `./b4w.sh` is the correct dev-mode invocation on Linux
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Unclear behavior of --endpoint combined with --cdp in attach command

sections.body: ./b4w.sh -s test attach --endpoint http://localhost:8182 --cdp chrome
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Output should indicate whether the CDP connection was routed through the remote Browser4 server or made directly.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Output says 'Attached to browser at http://localhost:9222' with no mention of the endpoint. The user cannot tell whether the endpoint was used for CDP discovery, ignored, or used only for subsequent commands.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The attach.md docs state: 'When --endpoint is used alone (without --cdp), it switches the CLI to the remote server for subsequent commands.' But when combined with --cdp, the semantics are ambiguous — does the endpoint proxy the CDP connection, or does --cdp connect directly and --endpoint just set the server URL for later? The output provides no visibility into this.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ — attach command handler and/or MCP tool dispatch for attach
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- When --endpoint is combined with --cdp, print a clear message like 'CDP discovery routed through endpoint http://...' or 'Connecting directly to CDP at ...; endpoint http://... set for subsequent commands'
- Update attach.md to explicitly describe the combined --endpoint + --cdp behavior
- Consider a --dry-run flag for attach that shows what would be connected without actually connecting
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: close/disconnect semantics differ by session type — not surfaced in close output

sections.body: Attach a session then run `close`.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The close output should clearly state what happened to the browser and the session.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Output says 'Disconnected from attached browser. The browser remains running.' This is good for CDP-attached sessions, but a user who started with `open` (which launches its own browser) might expect `close` to also kill the browser. The word 'close' implies termination, not disconnection.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The same command name ('close') has different semantics depending on session type, but the command output doesn't adapt to explain the distinction in all cases. The attach.md reference documents this well, but CLI output is the user's primary feedback channel.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ — close command output formatting
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Always include a one-line summary of what 'close' did for this session type: e.g., 'Browser process terminated' vs 'Disconnected — browser keeps running'
- Consider adding a `disconnect` alias prominently in help to signal the intent difference
- Show a tip on first `open` close: 'Tip: use attach to reconnect to existing browsers without launching a new one'
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: No confirmation prompt before closing a session with unsaved state

sections.body: Run `close` on a session after interacting with pages (e.g., filling forms, navigating).
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: A warning or confirmation prompt if there is unsaved browser state (cookies, localStorage, form data).
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: `close` disconnects immediately with no warning. Any unsaved authentication state, form progress, or cookies are lost.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The close command does not check whether state-save has been called recently or whether the session has accumulated meaningful state. There's no 'dirty' flag tracking state mutations.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ — close command handler
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Add a `--force` flag to skip confirmation, and prompt by default if the session has been active
- Or emit a tip after close: 'Tip: use state-save before close to preserve cookies and localStorage'
- Track a 'last-state-save' timestamp and warn if close is called with newer browser activity
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Short-flag PowerShell warning appears in bash context via b4w.sh

sections.body: ./b4w.sh -s eval-session snapshot -v 0 2>&1
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: No PowerShell-related warnings when using the bash wrapper.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Output begins with: ⚠ Short flags detected: -v / PowerShell may intercept these in other contexts (b4w.sh, direct pwsh). / Prefer long-form equivalents... This warning is confusing when running from a bash shell where PowerShell parameter binding is irrelevant.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: b4w.sh delegates to b4w.ps1 via pwsh. The warning is emitted by b4w.ps1 before it delegates to the CLI binary. It fires for any invocation, including those routed through b4w.sh where the bash wrapper should provide protection.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: b4w.ps1:39-47 — short-flag warning block
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Suppress the short-flag warning when invoked from b4w.sh (e.g., check an env var set by b4w.sh)
- Or reposition the warning to only show in interactive PowerShell sessions, not in piped/scripted contexts
- Add `--viewport` as a long-form equivalent in the help text for snapshot
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: snapshot -v 0 uses zero-based viewport indexing — counterintuitive

sections.body: ./b4w.sh snapshot -v 0
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Either 1-based viewport indexing, or clear documentation that viewports are 0-indexed.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: `-v 0` selects the first viewport (top chunk). While the SKILL.md comment '# -v 0 = top-of-page chunk' explains this, a new user encountering `-v 0` without reading the docs would likely guess `-v 1` for the first viewport. The output shows 'processingViewport: 0' which matches but doesn't explain the convention.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Zero-based indexing is common in programming but non-obvious to CLI users who expect 1-based counts for human-facing indices. The snapshot output uses 'viewport 0' consistently but there's no onboarding hint.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ — snapshot command help text
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Add a sentence to `snapshot --help`: 'Viewport indices are zero-based: -v 0 is the top of page, -v 1 is the next chunk'
- Consider accepting both -v 0 and -v 1 as the first viewport with a deprecation notice for the ambiguous form
- Add a tip on first snapshot invocation explaining viewport numbering
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: attach auto-captures snapshot on success — surprising for new users

sections.body: ./b4w.sh -s test attach --cdp chrome
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Attach command reports connection success and waits for the next command.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Attach automatically takes a snapshot and prints page URL, title, and snapshot file path. This is convenient but surprising — the output mixes connection status with page inspection, and a new user may be confused about whether 'attach' or 'snapshot' produced the snapshot.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The attach command includes an implicit snapshot as part of its post-attach flow. This is a deliberate convenience feature (the docs show 'Interact with your existing tabs → snapshot' as step 3 after attach), but it's not documented that attach does this automatically.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-rest/... — MCPToolController attach handler or backend attach flow
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Document in attach.md that a snapshot is auto-captured on successful attach
- Add a flag like `--no-snapshot` to skip the auto-snapshot
- Make the auto-snapshot more clearly delineated from the attach output (e.g., a separator or heading 'Auto-captured page state:')
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: tab-select by GUID requires --guid flag but help text doesn't show the syntax clearly

sections.body: ./b4w.sh help | grep 'tab-select'
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Help output should show both index-based and GUID-based selection syntax.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Help shows: `tab-select [index] [--guid <guid>]`. The bracket notation implies both are optional and position-independent, but a new user might try `tab-select C7FC...` (without --guid) and get an error. The SKILL.md correctly documents this but the CLI help is ambiguous.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The help text format `tab-select [index] [--guid <guid>]` uses standard CLI convention where [--guid <guid>] is a separate optional flag, but the `[index]` being first and `[--guid <guid>]` being second could be read as 'provide index then optionally --guid' rather than 'provide EITHER index OR --guid'.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ — tab-select command definition/help text
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Change help text to: `tab-select <index> | --guid <guid>` to indicate mutual exclusivity
- Or add usage examples to `tab-select --help`: 'tab-select 0' or 'tab-select --guid C7FC...'
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: b4w.sh rebuilds on every invocation even when binary is up to date

sections.body: Run any command via ./b4w.sh twice in succession.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Second invocation should skip the build step if sources haven't changed.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Every invocation shows 'Finished dev profile [unoptimized + debuginfo]' — while not a full rebuild (cargo detects no changes), it still takes ~0.4s of overhead per command. This is mild but adds friction to the interactive loop.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: b4w.sh uses `cargo run` or invokes the binary, but cargo still checks timestamps each time. With 10+ commands in a session, this adds 4+ seconds of perceived latency.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: b4w.sh — launcher script logic
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- The auto-build detection in b4w.ps1 (checking source timestamps vs binary) is good — ensure b4w.sh uses the same fast path
- Consider a `--no-build` flag to skip build checks entirely for rapid iteration
- Add an env var like B4W_SKIP_BUILD_CHECK=1 for power users
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
